notes:
ROUND 56. Two records filed (CPV, DZA). Country by country:

CPV (Cape Verde) -- SETTLED. Method 1 (bank's own publications index, fetched directly) worked. curl of https://www.bcv.cv/ then https://www.bcv.cv/pt/Estatisticas/Publicacoes%20e%20Intervencoes/Relatorios/Paginas/Relat%C3%B3rios.aspx (HTTP 200, 816 KB) carried the PDF paths inside a JavaScript data blob rather than in href attributes; grepping for 'SiteCollectionDocuments/' exposed the Relatorio e Contas series (RCA 2016.pdf ... Relatorio Conselho de Administracao 2024). Downloaded the FY2024 report (9.2 MB, 249 pp). Pages 246-249 are image-only scans that pdftotext returns blank, so they were rasterised with pdftoppm and OCRed with tesseract -l por: page 246 is the 'Relatorio do Auditor Independente' on EY letterhead, page 248 is the Conselho Fiscal's parecer which names 'EY Cabo Verde - Auditores e Consultores - Sociedade de Auditores Certificados' as the external auditor. Lesson for later rounds: a central bank report whose audit opinion grep comes back empty may simply have the opinion as a scanned image -- OCR the last few pages before logging an absence.

DZA (Algeria) -- RECORD FILED, but FLAGGED FOR THE OWNER'S JUDGEMENT. www.bank-of-algeria.dz remains unreachable from this sandbox, so the statute route was used instead. joradp.dz is reachable (the brief's suggestion was right). Walked the 2023 French-language Journal Officiel issues: F2023040/041/042 (200, no match; JO 42 of 25 June 2023 carries Loi 23-07 and 23-08 only) and then F2023043.pdf (200, 261 KB) which carries Loi n. 23-09 relative a la monnaie et au credit. Section 3 of that law is headed 'Surveillance et controle de la Banque d'Algerie par le Censorat'. Article 29 creates a Censorat of two censeurs appointed by presidential decree, full-time, who must have central-bank accounting knowledge. Article 30 says they carry out whatever verifications they judge appropriate, report to the board on the verification of the year-end accounts ('les verifications des comptes de fin d'exercice'), and send a report to the Minister of Finance within four months of the close of the financial year. So Algeria's statutory verifier of the central bank's own accounts is a NAMED BODY, not a mere mechanism -- which is why it is filed -- but it is an organ created by the bank's own charter law and its members sit in board sessions with a consultative voice, so it sits close to the 'audited by its own supervisory board' pattern the brief treats as a structural blank. If the owner reads the Censorat as internal, this record should be dropped and DZA reclassified as a structural blank with the statute citation above as the evidence. No private firm is named anywhere in Loi 23-09 for the bank's own accounts (the 'commissaires aux comptes' articles later in the law, around the centrale des risques provisions, bind commercial banks and financial institutions, not the Banque d'Algerie).

KHM (Cambodia) -- GENUINE ABSENCE / MECHANISM ONLY. nbc.gov.kh/english/economic_research/annual_report.php returned HTTP 403. Routed around it: the full English NBC Annual Report 2024 (158 pp, 12 MB) is mirrored on Open Development Cambodia at https://data.opendevelopmentcambodia.net/km/dataset/b96877c9-a821-4010-9c4a-87297b08f82c/resource/586b948b-b560-4d47-a8ca-1b8ade6a7733/download/ar_eng_as_of_16.07.25_clean.pdf (HTTP 200). pdftotext gives clean text. ZERO hits for 'independent auditor', 'external audit', Deloitte, KPMG, PwC, Ernst, Grant Thornton, BDO or National Audit Authority. Every 'audit' hit is internal audit and inspection. The only governance hit is at the 162nd board meeting of 24 January 2024, which approved 'the draft for establishing the audit committee to inspect the NBC's accounting records for 2023' -- a board-appointed committee, i.e. a mechanism naming nobody. The NBC does not publish an auditor's name in its own annual report. Recommend reclassifying KHM as a structural blank unless a Cambodian gazette route turns up.

CUW (Curacao) -- HOST BLOCK, WORSE THAN LAST ROUND. The per-year index pages could not be opened. WebFetch of https://exch.centralbank.cw/annual-reports-quarterly-bulletins/2024 now fails with 'robots_disallowed' -- the host's robots.txt blocks the fetcher, so the WebFetch route the brief recorded as working is closed. curl of the same URL fails on TLS ('could not establish a secure connection', exit with HTTP 000), the certificate subject-name mismatch the brief describes. https://www.centralbank.cw/annual-reports returns HTTP 403. One real gain: the correct path shape includes a /publications/ segment the brief's paths omitted, e.g. https://exch.centralbank.cw/publications/annual-reports-quarterly-bulletins/2021/condensed-financial-statements-as-of-december-31-2020 -- WebFetch did retrieve that one (it predates the robots change in the cache) and it names no firm and carries no document link in its markup; the PDF is behind a link with no visible href. Next round should try the /publications/ year indexes through a real browser rather than curl or WebFetch.

RWA (Rwanda) -- STILL DEAD. https://www.bnr.rw/index.php?id=82 (the legacy-style URL that search engines index) returns HTTP 200 but is the same React shell: the body is literally 'You need to enable JavaScript to run this app', behind Cloudflare. Statute route tried and failed: no copy of Law 48/2017 governing the National Bank of Rwanda was reachable; https://www.parliament.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/Parliament/Resources/Bills_Before_Parliament/Draft_Law_governing_BNR.pdf returns HTTP 404 with an HTML error body. Two targeted searches for a BNR audit opinion returned only Rwandan commercial banks (BPR, BOA Rwanda, NCBA Rwanda, KCB Rwanda, Access Bank Rwanda) -- exactly the failure mode the brief warns about. Untried and worth a round: archive.gazettes.africa, which does hold Rwandan government gazettes (an unrelated 2021 special issue surfaced), and the Rwanda Office of the Auditor General's own annual report listing audited entities.

MRT (Mauritania) -- HOST BLOCK CONFIRMED. https://www.bcm.mr/ returns HTTP 200 with 2,568 bytes, the single-page-app shell the brief describes. No further route attempted this round.

PRY (Paraguay) -- NOT SETTLED, NO RECENT TENDER FOUND. The .csv trick was never reached because no recent Banco Central del Paraguay external-audit adjudicacion path could be identified. Two searches of contrataciones.gov.py / DNCP for a BCP 'auditoria externa' award returned only opaque /api/resultado/<uuid>/files/<uuid>/download links (which are undocumented API paths and were deliberately not probed, per instruction) plus convocatoria 438702, which is 'adquisicion software gestion auditorias' -- audit-management software, not an audit engagement. A third search for a BCP audit opinion naming a Big Four firm returned only Paraguayan commercial banks (ueno, Atlas, GNB, Citibank Paraguay). bcp.gov.py was not re-tried; the brief records /estados-financieros-i367 as 403 behind a WAF. Next round needs the DNCP search UI (JavaScript, so a browser) to get a convocatoria id before the .csv trick can be applied.

BLR (Belarus) -- NOT ATTEMPTED AS A FETCH. Given six prior HTTP 000 failures on nbrb.by from this network, only a Russian-language search was run; it returned Belarusian commercial banks (MTBank, Paritetbank, TC Bank, Belvnesheconombank) and Kazakh/Kyrgyz central banks, no NBRB audit opinion. pravo.by was not reached. Note for the next round: the Belarusian Banking Code provision on the National Bank's annual report is expected to name only a mechanism (an audit organisation determined by the President), which would not be a record.

MWI (Malawi) -- NOT SETTLED. https://www.rbm.mw/Publications/AnnualReports/ returns HTTP 200 (89 KB) three ways but the report list is injected by JavaScript; the only PDFs in the markup are the three Access to Information Act documents. One request returned HTTP 000 and succeeded on retry, so the host does reset at random as the brief warns. A search for an RBM 2024 auditor's report returned only Malawian commercial banks (CDH, National Bank of Malawi, First Capital, Standard Bank Malawi) plus the Scribd page the brief already rejected. Read https://mwnation.com/rbm-chalks-k356bnprofit-results-show/ (HTTP 200, 127 KB) in full: it reports the K356bn profit from the 2024 financial statements but contains no occurrence of 'audit' or of any firm name, so it is not even a weak_source. Deloitte was NOT filed, per instruction.

PSE (Palestine) -- HOST IS A JAVASCRIPT SHELL. https://www.pma.ps/en/Publications/AnnualReports returns HTTP 200 but only 6,300 bytes: a Vite/React shell whose only hrefs are favicons, a CSS bundle and Google Fonts. No document list in the markup. Two searches returned PMA press releases about older annual reports and unrelated Palestinian commercial banks, no audit opinion. Needs a browser or a mirror (info.wafa.ps hosts some PMA PDFs and is worth a try next round).

LAO (Laos) -- HOST UNREACHABLE. https://www.bol.gov.la/en/ and https://www.bol.gov.la/en/annual_report both returned HTTP 000 with zero bytes from this sandbox. Not a scan, a network-level failure.

TKM (Turkmenistan) and YEM (Yemen) -- NOT ATTEMPTED this round; the fetch budget went to the leads above. No new information.

No record was keyed to ECB, EMU, BCEAO, BEAC or ECCB.

records.detail: EY's Cape Verde member firm signed the Relatorio do Auditor Independente on the Banco de Cabo Verde's financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024, giving an unqualified opinion on a balance sheet total of 99,898,332 thousand escudos and negative equity of 622,855 thousand escudos; the engagement is confirmed a second time in the Conselho Fiscal's Relatorio e Parecer in the same report, issued under article 47(1) of the bank's Lei Organica, which records that the council reviewed the opinion expressed in the external audit report carried out by EY Cabo Verde.

records.detail: Algeria names no audit firm for the Banque d'Algerie's own accounts: under section 3 of Loi n. 23-09 of 21 June 2023 relative a la monnaie et au credit, published in Journal Officiel n. 43 of 27 June 2023, oversight of the bank is carried out by a Censorat of two censeurs appointed by presidential decree who must hold central-bank accounting expertise (article 29), and article 30 requires them to report to the board on their verification of the year-end accounts and to send a report to the Minister of Finance within four months of the close of each financial year, the accounts themselves being closed on 31 December under article 31.
records.as_of: Loi 23-09 of 21 June 2023, in force for financial years from 2023
